original: The Progressive Conservatives brought an emergency two hour debate to the floor Wednesday to discuss the current shortage of family doctors and the decision by the new health authority to limit how many doctors can work at walk-in clinics or set up shop in the Halifax area.
sampled:
The motion to have debate on Bill 148, The Health Care Financing Act, was carried unanimously. The Opposition parties on the health committee had been lobbying the Speaker for an emergency debate.

Bill 148 proposes a major shift in health-care funding in Nova Scotia, and is intended to make health care sustainable for years to come. The new health authority, which took over the provincial health-care system on July 1, is responsible for paying doctors under the new arrangement. The new authority has set a ceiling on the number of primary care physicians that can work in Halifax and Dartmouth. The new authority has also said the cap would remain at the cap until the new authority has sufficient resources and the capacity to expand.

Bill 148 has also led to a major shift in who is responsible for paying doctors under the new arrangement. The new authority, and the provincial government, is responsible for paying doctors under the new arrangement, but not the individual doctors. The doctors are now responsible for paying their own health-care expenses. The new arrangement is a major change for physicians who have had direct access to Nova Scotia’s health-care system.
